name: Question 5
problem:
| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=3$ | $Y=5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=2$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.15$ | $0.05$ | $0.15$ |
| $X=6$ | $0.2$ | $0$ | $0.05$ |

Compute $P(X=4\,|\,Y=3)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above. Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
worked_solution:
By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by

$$
P(X=4\,|\,Y=3)=\frac{P(X=4,Y=3)}{P(Y=3)}=\frac{f(4,3)}{{f}_{Y}(3)},
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(3) & =f(2,3)+f(4,3)+f(6,3) \\  & =0.1+0.05+0 \\  & =0.15.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(4,3)=0.05.$ 

Finally, substituting ${f}_{Y}(3)=0.15$ and $f(4,3)=0.05$ in our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=4\,|\,Y=3) & =\frac{f(4,3)}{{f}_{Y}(3)} \\  & =\frac{0.05}{0.15} \\  & =0.33.\end{aligned}
$$

Compute P(X=4|Y=3) given that the discrete random variables X and Y have the joint probability mass function f(x,y) shown in the table above. Round your answer to 2 decimal places.

EXPLANATION

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by P(X=4|Y=3)=P(X=4,Y=3)P(Y=3)=f(4,3)fY(3), where f(x,y) is the joint probability mass function of X and Y, and fY(y) is the marginal distribution of Y.

Recall that the marginal distribution for Y corresponds to the column totals. Thus, fY(3)=f(2,3)+f(4,3)+f(6,3)=0.1+0.05+0=0.15.

From the given table, we have that f(4,3)=0.05.

Finally, substituting fY(3)=0.15 and f(4,3)=0.05 in our formula above, we obtain P(X=4|Y=3)=f(4,3)fY(3)=0.050.15=0.33.
